question: Which statement best describes createPortal signature?
options: ReactDOM.createPortal(children, container) takes the React children to render and an existing DOM node to render them into, and returns a React node you return from your component like any JSX. The container must already exist in the document when the portal renders — you typically reference document.body or a dedicated <div id="modal-root"> placed in your HTML. It is the only API you need to teleport DOM.

A portal changes only where the children's DOM physically lands; it does NOT move them in the React component tree. They remain logical descendants of the component that declared the portal, which is why props, state, and context all continue to flow normally. This decoupling — declared in one place, rendered in another — is the entire point of portals.

Events from a portaled component bubble up through the React tree (where the portal is declared), not the DOM tree where the nodes physically live. So a click inside a portal triggers onClick handlers on the React ancestor that rendered it, even though in the DOM those nodes sit under document.body. This surprises many developers and is a classic interview gotcha — note that native addEventListener on document still follows the real DOM tree.

The primary reason portals exist: overlays rendered inline get clipped by an ancestor's overflow:hidden, trapped in a low z-index stacking context, or distorted by a CSS transform. Rendering into a top-level container moves the overlay's DOM outside those ancestors entirely, so none of those constraints apply. Reaching for ever-higher z-index is the wrong fix; escaping the stacking context is the right one.

These are the canonical portal use cases — any floating overlay that must visually sit above the rest of the page. They share a need to escape ancestor clipping and to overlay the full viewport (usually with position:fixed). Co-locating the trigger logic with the component while portaling the DOM lets you keep modal state local instead of hoisting it to the app root.

question: Which statement best describes Event bubbling through the React tree?

Because portal events bubble through the React parent, a common bug is that clicking inside a modal closes it — the click bubbles up to a backdrop or outside-click handler. The fix is to call e.stopPropagation() on the inner dialog content so inner clicks don't reach the backdrop's onClick. This is a direct consequence of the React-tree event behavior.

createPortal moves DOM but does nothing for accessibility — you own that. An accessible modal must move focus into the dialog on open, trap Tab/Shift+Tab within it, restore focus to the trigger element on close, close on Escape, and set ARIA roles (role="dialog", aria-modal="true", aria-labelledby). Headless libraries like Radix UI, Headless UI, and react-aria provide these dialog primitives built on portals so you don't hand-roll focus trapping.
